----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Mahendra Singh Yadav with Mr. Jai Prakash Bulania For Respondent(s) :

Mr. Narendra Kumar Jain HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MAHENDAR KUMAR GOYAL Order 18/01/2023 This writ petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India is directed against the order dated 18.11.2019 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhunjhunu (for brevity "the learned Tribunal") in Claim Case No.314/2016 whereby, evidence of the petitioners/claimants has been closed.

The relevant facts in brief are that the petitioners filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (2 of 3) [CW-2798/2020] (hereinafter referred to as "the Act of 1988")
before the learned Tribunal seeking compensation on account of death of Shri Anil Kumar, their son.
During the course of proceedings, the learned Tribunal, vide its order dated 18.11.2019, closed right of the claimants to lead their evidence.
Assailing the order, learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that on account of unavoidable circumstances, they could not lead their evidence.
He submits that they may be granted only one opportunity to lead their evidence in the interest of justice.

He, therefore, prays that the writ petition be allowed, the order dated 18.11.2019 be quashed and set aside and they may be granted one Basesar Son Of Shri Mala vs Jagpal Singh Son Of Shri Dhanraj Singh on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84025034/
1 opportunity to lead their evidence.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that evidence of the petitioners was closed when despite availing sufficient opportunities, they failed to lead the same.
He submits that the order dated 18.11.2019 does not warrant any interference by this Court.

He, further submits that in any case, if this Court is inclined to extend the petitioners an opportunity to lead their evidence, the interest of Insurance Company should be protected and the petitioner should not be held entitled for the interest for the period of delay on account of their fault.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that they are ready to forego the interest, if any, for the period from 18.11.2019 till the date they are permitted to lead their evidence in case they are granted an opportunity to lead their evidence.
Heard.
Considered.
The claim petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking compensation on account of death of their son, a young boy of 19 years of age.

Their evidence was closed by the learned Tribunal (3 of 3)
[CW-2798/2020] vide order impugned as they failed to lead the same despite availing a number of opportunities.

However, in the interest of justice and keeping in view of the provisions of the Act of 1988, a beneficial piece of legislation in favour of the claimants, this Court deems it just and proper to grant the petitioners one opportunity to lead their evidence.

In view thereof, this writ petition is allowed in following terms:
1. The order dated 18.11.2019 passed by the learned Tribunal in Claim Case No.341/2016 is quashed and set aside.
2.
The petitioners are given one opportunity of lead their entire evidence either on the next date fixed before the learned Tribunal or within 15 days thereafter, if the learned Tribunal so directs.

3. The petitioners shall not be entitled for any interest on the compensation amount,
if any, for the period from 18.11.2019 till the date they lead evidence.

(MAHENDAR KUMAR GOYAL),J Manish/55 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
